title: Vivienne Jolie-Pitt Files to Drop Father's Surname, Fourth Sibling to Do So
excerpt: The 18-year-old daughter of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt filed a petition in Los Angeles County Superior Court on July 21, joining siblings Shiloh, Maddox, and Zahara in seeking to legally remove 'Pitt' from her name.
body:
• Vivienne Jolie-Pitt has filed a petition to change her name, dropping her father's surname, which is set for a court hearing on November 2.
  • She is the fourth child of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt to seek this name change, following siblings Maddox, Zahara, and Shiloh.
  • The name changes reflect a broader trend among the siblings, with only Pax still using the full Jolie-Pitt surname.
  • The petitions are seen as a response to the fallout from their parents' contentious divorce.

Vivienne Jolie-Pitt has filed a petition in Los Angeles County Superior Court to legally change her name from Vivienne Marcheline Jolie-Pitt to Vivienne Marcheline Jolie. The 18-year-old, who signed the petition on her birthday on July 12, cited "personal" reasons for the request, according to court documents reviewed by People and Entertainment Weekly. A hearing is scheduled for November 2.

Vivienne is the fourth of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt's six children to formally seek to remove the actor's surname. The filing comes just weeks after her older siblings Maddox, 24, and Zahara, 21, submitted similar petitions. Shiloh, now 20, first filed on her 18th birthday in May 2024 and has since had her name change granted.

A Family Moving in One Direction

The pattern is unmistakable. Maddox filed in May to become Maddox Chivan Jolie. Zahara followed in June, requesting to be known as Zahara Marley Jolie — a name she had already been using since joining Alpha Kappa Alpha sorority at Spelman College in 2023. Hearings for their petitions are set for September 14 and September 28, respectively.

Vivienne had already signaled her preference. When she co-produced the Broadway musical The Outsiders with her mother in 2024, the Playbill listed her simply as Vivienne Jolie. Twin brother Knox, 18, reportedly omitted "Pitt" from his high school diploma when he graduated in Los Angeles on June 5. Only Pax, 22, still legally carries the full Jolie-Pitt surname.

"If people knew the whole truth, they would have more sympathy for the children and respect them. The fact they aren't speaking ill or sharing things publicly only shows their decency."

— Source close to Angelina Jolie, speaking to People

Dueling Narratives

The name changes have become a proxy for the broader fallout from one of Hollywood's most bitter divorces. Jolie filed for divorce from Pitt in September 2016 after two years of marriage. The pair were declared legally single in 2019, but their divorce was not finalized until December 2024 — more than eight years after the split.

A source close to Jolie told People on July 22 that the actress "hasn't been fighting and isn't angry. She just wants everyone to heal." A source close to Pitt offered a starkly different reading, telling People earlier that it was "sad to see someone repeatedly publicize their successful alienation of their children from the other parent."

A separate source close to Pitt told USA Today that "it is important to contextualize that Brad was awarded 50/50 custody of the children in 2021 following lengthy testimonies from witnesses, experts, therapists and other people who had been with the kids and around them." USA Today noted that the judge who issued that 2021 custody ruling was later disqualified by a California appeals court for failing to disclose professional relationships with Pitt's attorneys.

What It Means Beyond Hollywood

For the Indian diaspora, where surnames carry deep familial and cultural weight, the Jolie-Pitt children's collective decision underscores a universal tension between identity, loyalty, and autonomy. Angelina Jolie's humanitarian profile across South Asia — from her years as a UNHCR Special Envoy to her advocacy for refugees — has made her a familiar figure in Indian media, lending this family story an added layer of resonance.

In California, a name change petition by an adult is a relatively straightforward legal process. The petitioner must be at least 18 years old, file the request with the superior court, and attend a hearing. Absent any objections, these petitions are routinely granted.

What's Next

Vivienne's hearing is set for November 2. Maddox's and Zahara's hearings are scheduled for September. If all three are granted, five of Brad Pitt's six children will have either legally changed their names or publicly distanced themselves from his surname. Neither Jolie nor Pitt has commented publicly on the filings.
